name: Boggard (Far Distant Future Publishing)
body:
Boggards are a race of froglike humanoids that typically live in swamps and are almost universally disliked by their neighbors. They are known by many different names, but boggard is the most common—and one of the few polite enough to print.

Physical

Boggards resemble anthropomorphic frogs or toads. They have smooth skin, webbed hands and feet, wide mouths, and bulging eyes. They come in many variations, but typically have green, gray or mottled yellow skin to help blend into the swamp. They have long, flicking tongues that never sit still and can barely stay out of the way of their words as they talk.

As boggards age, they continue to grow larger and fatter, and their coloration becomes duller, sometimes even fading to white. The wisest among these elder boggards are known as “priest-kings,” and are given wide berth as the ruling caste among boggards.

Social

When most people think of boggards, they think of the cruel beings that establish demon-worshipping colonies in the heart of swamps or near riverbanks. These common boggards take pleasure in needless violence, capturing and sacrificing other humanoids to their dark gods.

Boggards are a scourge upon any land they inhabit. They reproduce rapidly and hunt, kill, and forage indiscriminately, soon depleting the area of its resources. The boggards inevitably turn to raiding neighboring settlements (and often infighting among themselves) in order to survive.

Boggards begin their lives as tadpoles, becoming terrestrial around the age of 3 years. They are accepted into the tribe as soon as they complete their first hunt or raid, which comes soon after.

Alignment and Religion

Most common boggards are Chaotic Evil.

They are cruel, hedonistic, and wantonly destructive, and their worship of demons only serves to reinforce these instincts. However, while this is the common perception of boggards, there are actually many varieties of these frogfolk that people are less familiar with. Chaotic alignments do seem to predominate, as all boggards prefer their freedom and autonomy, but some—like the fey boggards—are full of whimsy and mischief, rather than cruelty, while others merely wish to live their own lives and be left alone.

Names

Some typical names for boggards include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Aooga
Borgorup
Boruup
Breebeeg
Eepa
Eereep
Gogurp
Kreek
Orogora
Raab
Ribbap
Urpa
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are brawny and rugged, but slow in both body and mind. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con, –2 Dex, –2 Int [specialized, penalty]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the boggard subtype. (0)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. Your speed is never modified by armor or encumbrance. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Boggard. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Aklo, Common, Draconic, Elven, Grippli, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Hold Breath You can hold your breath for a number of rounds equal to four times your Constitution score before you risk drowning or suffocating. (1)
Jumper You are always considered to have a running start when making Athletics checks to jump. (2)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor You have tough, rubbery skin that provides a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Swamp Stride You can move through difficult terrain at your normal speed while in swampy or marshy terrain. Magically altered terrain affects you normally. (1)
Swim You have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 species bonus on Swim checks that a swim speed normally grants. (2)
Sticky Tongue You can make melee attacks with your long, sticky tongue. This is a secondary natural attack. A creature hit by this attack cannot move more than 10 feet away from you and takes a –2 penalty to AC as long as the tongue is attached (this penalty does not stack if multiple tongues are attached). The tongue can be removed by the target or an adjacent ally by making an opposed Strength check against you as a standard action or by dealing 2 points of damage to your tongue (AC 11, damage does not reduce your hit points). You cannot move more than 10 feet away from a creature stuck to your tongue, but you can release your tongue from the target as a free action. You can only have one creature attached to your tongue at a time. (2)
Terrifying Croak Once per hour as a standard action, you can emit a thunderous croak. Any creature within 30 feet of you, other than another boggard, must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 your level + your Constitution modifier) or become shaken for 1d4 rounds. Creatures that are already shaken become frightened for 1 round, plus have the duration of the shaken effect extended by 1d4 rounds. A creature that succeeds at this save cannot be affected by the same boggard’s terrifying croak again for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting sonic fear effect. (2)
Total: 15 RP (Advanced)
Variants
Fey Boggard Variant

Some boggards are strongly influenced by the fey elements of the swamps in which they dwell. These boggards are notable for their particularly round bodies and long, thin legs. Unlike common boggards, fey boggard society encourages its people to always maintain their appearance with the finest clothing and latest styles. Fey boggards do not believe there is anything as being overdressed for an occasion!

Despite their somewhat fragile and foppish appearance, however, they are surprisingly strong and durable, and just as dangerous as common boggards if provoked.

Fey boggards have a keen sense of orderliness, and have developed a culture built around personal etiquette. They jockey for titles of aristocracy, and even minor awards and recognitions are displayed with great pride. Their bravest warriors become knights who defend the bullywug code of chivalry and honor, while being clad in the finest armor and seated atop the stoutest toad steeds. Of course, what passes for proper behavior for a fey boggard is sometimes strange, amusing, or downright confusing for humanoids—if not outright dangerous. A fey boggard’s interaction with others, especially humanoids that pass through their swamps, is usually centered around trade, as they enjoy obtaining finery and shiny things. However, these interactions do sometimes result in misunderstandings—usually from perceived breaches of etiquette—that sometimes result in the arrest of strangers, who must then be brought before the bullywug monarch for judgment.

Fey Heritage Your type changes to fey, and your ability scores modifiers become +4 Cha, +2 Str, +2 Dex, +2 Con, –2 Int. This trait alters type and ability score modifiers, and replaces natural armor and sticky tongue.

Spell-Like Croak Select one of the following spells: charm person, command, compel hostility, ear-piercing scream, or lesser confusion. Once chosen, this selection cannot be changed. Once per day, you can unleash a croak at a single target within 30 feet and affect it as per the spell chosen. Treat this as a spell-like ability, except that it has a verbal component and a 30-foot range. This trait replaces terrifying croak.

Priest-King Boggard

Usually, only older boggards develop into priest-kings, but sometimes younger specimens can develop these qualities if raised on a special diet of blue dragonfly pulp.

Ability Score Modifiers Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Wis. This trait alters ability score modifiers and replaces jumper.
Spell-Like Abilities You can use fog cloud, jump, and summon swarm once per day each as spell-like abilities, using your character level as the caster level and Charisma as your casting ability. This trait replaces sticky tongue and swamp stride.
Alternate Species Traits
Amphibious You and can breathe both air and water. This trait replaces hold breath and low-light vision.
Bogbiter Some varieties of boggards have enlarged teeth in their upper jaws. You gain a bite attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 damage. This trait replaces terrifying croak.
Frogspeech You gain speak with animals as a constant spell-like ability, except that it only functions with frogs and toads (including giant versions of these creatures). This trait replaces hold breath. Ghostfrog Boggards naturally lose their coloring as they age, turning pale with age. However, some few are born as albinos or with other strange markings that indicate from birth that they belong to the ruing caste. These “ghost frogs” often have unexplained powers that prove their status.
As a ghost frog, you can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Intelligence modifier for all Intelligence-based class sills, and you can use the following spell-like abilities once each per day: hydraulic push, obscuring mist, and water walk. Your character level is your caster level, and Charisma is your casting ability. This trait replaces hold breath, swamp stride, and swim.
Motion Camouflage You can use blurred movement once per day as a spell-like ability, using your character level as the caster level. This trait replaces swamp stride.
Swamp Camouflage You gain a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks while in swamp or marsh terrain. This trait replaces swamp stride.
Toadsong Boggards, like grippli, often communicate across the swamps and fens by means of throat vocalizations. A practitioner of toadsong can utter 6 words in Boggard every round that carry across surprising distances: 400 feet indoors, and four times that outdoors. Unless a being actually has Boggard on their list of languages they will not recognize toadsong as sentient communication, and cannot, in any case, locate the source of the sound. You can use toadsong a number of rounds per day equal to your Constitution score. This trait replaces hold breath.
Warhopper When boggards go to war, it is the warhoppers that lead the charge, leaping into battle. By making an Acrobatics check (DC 15), you can make a 5-foot step that is actually 10 feet instead of 5, without drawing an attack of opportunity. If the check fails you fall prone. This trait replaces sticky tongue.
Species Feats
Exploding Warts

Those who dare assault your mystical warts pay an awful price.

Prerequisites: boggard.

Benefit: Whenever an opponent scores a critical hit against you with a melee attack (excluding melee weapons that have the reach quality), a wart explodes in their face and deals acid damage equal to 1d6 + your character level (Reflex half; DC 10 + 1/2 your character level + your Constitution modifier).

Marshmaster

In the swamp, boggards rule all!

Prerequisite(s): boggard; swamp stride ancestry trait; any one of Great Fortitude, Iron Will, or Lightning Reflexes.

Benefit: You gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC and a +2 competence bonus to initiative checks and Perception checks whenever you are in swamp or marsh terrain.

Reckless Summoning

Boggard clerics are notorious for their powerful but unpredictable summoning abilities.

Prerequisites: ability to cast any summon monster spell, boggard.

Benefit: Any time you cast a summon monster spell, there is a 50% chance that one more creature than the spell would ordinarily summon will appear. In such cases, however, there is a 25% chance that the creatures summoned will not be under your control, rampaging and attacking all targets within sight at random, including you.

Special: Note that boggard casters often take this feat despite its dangers, and it is not uncommon for boggards that have summoned monsters to spend all their efforts fighting their own summoned creatures instead of their original foe. A defeat under such circumstances is not considered shameful, but merely the will of the gods.

Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1/2 to your bomb damage.
Antipaladin Add +1/2 hit point to your touch of corruption ability (whether using it to heal or harm).
Barbarian Add +1 on your Acrobatics checks to jump.
Bard Reduce the amount of time you must wait before using your terrifying croak species ability by 5 minutes (to a minimum of 5 minutes).
Cleric Add +1/2 to damage dealt when channeling energy (whether positive or negative).
Druid Add a +1/2 bonus on concentration checks to cast druid spells. This bonus doubles in a swamp terrain.
Fighter Increase the hit points of your sticky tongue ability by +1 and add +1/2 on all opposed Strength checks to prevent a creature from detaching your sticky tongue.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or trip maneuver.
Ranger Add +1/4 to a single existing favored terrain bonus (maximum +2 per favored terrain).
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception and Stealth checks while in a swamp.
Skald Reduce the amount of time you must wait before using your terrifying croak species ability by 5 minutes (to a minimum of 5 minutes).
Sorcerer Add +1/2 to the number of times per day you can use the protoplasm protean bloodline power, or +1 to the total number of rounds per day you can use the claws abyssal bloodline power. You must possess the applicable power to select these bonuses.
Summoner Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of your summon monster spell-like ability.
Warpriest Gain a +1/3 bonus on the damage dealt with your channel energy ability.
Witch Add one spell from the witch spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
